title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 26, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: mastra-ai/mastra is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: mastra-ai/mastra leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: mastra-ai/mastra — 8 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 41.1 below its current daily pace, with 10 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 146 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
earendil-works/pi — No same-day commit after 104 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Check the boundary behind a successful Studio tool call
dailyInsight.insight: Unsloth has merged a replacement OS sandbox, but automatic mode can still run with software safeguards when isolation is unavailable.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The planner records requested and effective modes separately. The tool wrapper preserves refusal for unsafe working folders and construction failures, while recording a separate path for user-approved host access.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A completed Python or Terminal command does not establish which filesystem boundary protected the host. Operators need the execution record and a test of their actual configuration.

actions.audience: Operators evaluating the new Unsloth Studio sandbox source
actions.label: Compare harmless canaries with the execution record
actions.instruction: In a disposable environment, identify the pinned build and execution mode. Compare an allowed working-folder operation with an outside read of a harmless canary that the host can read. Inspect effective mode, OS-isolation flag and limitations. Do not use real credentials or weaken host policy to force a pass.
actions.effort: One focused test session after installing the pinned build

receipts.title: Linux and macOS replacement sandbox
receipts.supports: Restores the planner, platform backends and execution-record distinction after the previous implementation was reverted.

receipts.title: Windows Preview integration and shared launch policy
receipts.supports: Adds capability-probed MXC integration with explicit Preview limits and launch/cleanup records.

confidence.basis: Merged planner and tool-wrapper branches agree with the narrowed claim; public reviews document why availability, refusal and fallback must be distinguished.

dailyInsight.limitation: We inspected source and public review evidence but did not run kernel-confinement tests or verify a released build. Linux/macOS network egress is not confined by this layer; Windows network posture remains unverified.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call if the pinned implementation no longer permits software-only automatic execution or runtime evidence contradicts the reported effective-mode record.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Request and interface wiring that makes each actual tool boundary visible to the user, plus platform-specific confinement results for released builds.

attentionQueue.note: At most three projects survive the morning filter. A receipt is required; movement alone is not a story.
